technical_and_design_decisions: Target one specific Hyperledger Fabric release and implement the library against that release's protobuf messages, configuration hierarchy, policies, capabilities, and serialization behavior.

Extend the transaction read-set representation to carry the value observed for each read key, in addition to the key and version, and update validation to compare the endorsed value with the committing peer's current world-state value.
Treat a value mismatch, missing key, or version mismatch as transaction invalidation; preserve the existing version-based MVCC checks.
Keep the configuration-generation library independent of Viper, YAML parsing, filesystem conventions, MSP directory layouts, and network access.
Accept cryptographic material and signing identities through explicit function parameters or interfaces rather than deriving them from configuration or local filesystem paths.

Use Fabric protobuf types and canonical deterministic protobuf serialization wherever possible so generated blocks and configuration updates are semantically equivalent to Fabric command-line tooling.

Implement detached signing as signing of the canonical configuration-update bytes and implement transaction assembly by preserving the supplied signature identities and signature bytes in Fabric's expected order-independent structure.

Implement configuration-difference calculation by using Fabric's configuration group update semantics, including added, modified, and deleted values and groups, rather than performing a generic protobuf diff.
Keep channel update generation and consortium organization addition unsigned, returning transactions that callers can subsequently sign.
Include unit tests, protobuf equality or semantic-equivalence tests, and integration-style fixture tests against representative output from configtxgen, cryptogen, configtxlator, and signtx.
assumptions: The work is performed by one experienced Go developer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals and protobuf-based APIs.
A single Fabric source tree and target release are available locally, including the relevant generated protobuf code and existing command implementations for reference.
The increment may change the transaction protobuf/API and does not need wire compatibility with peers from older Fabric releases unless explicitly covered by existing tests.

The exact behavior required by U1 is to detect tampering of an endorsing peer's read values at validation time; solving unrelated Byzantine endorsement or peer-authentication problems is out of scope.
Existing Fabric cryptographic providers, signing primitives, policy structures, and protobuf definitions can be reused rather than reimplemented.
Representative configtx.yaml, MSP, cryptographic-material, and command-output fixtures are available or can be created locally for testing.
No production deployment, operational rollout, performance benchmarking, or migration of existing ledger data is included.
The requested functions are delivered as a reusable Go package with public APIs, error handling, and basic documentation.

Generated output must match the target Fabric tooling semantically or by proto.Equal where the acceptance criteria explicitly require it; harmless nondeterministic signature ordering is normalized where Fabric permits it.
Normal code review, local debugging, and test execution are included in the estimates, but external review delays and calendar waiting time are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the target Fabric release, trace proposal read-set creation and commit-time validation, study configuration-generation command paths, define public APIs, identify protobuf and compatibility impacts, and prepare representative test fixtures.

activities.activity_name: Read-set value propagation and tamper validation
activities.activity_description: Modify the read-set data model and proposal-response serialization to include observed values, propagate values through chaincode execution and endorsement, and update peer validation to compare endorsed values with local world state while retaining MVCC checks.

Add unit and integration tests covering untampered reads, altered values, altered versions, missing keys, multiple endorsers, invalid transactions, ledger commit behavior, and serialization or upgrade edge cases.

activities.activity_name: Reusable configuration model and protobuf utility layer
activities.activity_description: Copy and adapt the required configuration structures without Viper or YAML dependencies, implement conversion helpers, canonical marshaling, policy and capability handling, and common configuration-group construction utilities.

Implement U2's channel specification types and CreateChannelTx function, construct the channel configuration and genesis block, support orderer, application, consortium, policy, and capability data, and validate against configtxgen fixtures.
Implement U3's explicit-key signing API, canonicalize the ChannelUpdate payload, produce the expected detached Fabric signature, and test verification with supplied identities and keys.

Implement U4's function to combine a ConfigUpdate transaction with detached signatures, construct the complete envelope and signature headers, and compare validation and output semantics with signatures added by signtx.

Implement U5's unsigned update builder, locate and modify the orderer batch-size value, calculate the corresponding configuration update, build the envelope, and test against manually generated tool output.

Implement U6's organization-group builder using directly supplied MSP identifiers, certificates, anchors, policies, and endpoints, and validate semantic equivalence with cryptogen and configtxgen -printOrg output.

Implement U7's base-versus-modified configuration comparison, including recursive group, value, and policy additions, modifications, and deletions, and produce a ConfigUpdate equivalent to configtxlator compute_update.

Implement U8's system-channel update that inserts an organization definition into a named consortium, reuse organization and configuration-difference helpers, and validate the unsigned result against the documented manual workflow.

Build reusable fixtures and integration tests covering all U2-U8 APIs, protobuf equality and semantic comparisons, signature verification, malformed-input errors, repeated updates, and regression behavior across supported configuration variants.
Document public types, function contracts, signing and key-material expectations, error behavior, unsigned-versus-signed workflows, and provide examples for channel creation and consortium updates.

activities.activity_name: Build integration and final quality pass
activities.activity_description: Integrate package changes with the repository build, update generated code or build scripts as required, run formatting and static analysis, fix final defects, and verify the complete test suite.
